defect.statement: network/lease-gas-owner.mjs renewalsFor/renewsPerDay/costModel/budgetAmount counted every lease as 'one renew per leaseSec' (48/day at 1800 s). The deployed ledger rev 16d _burnLease sets until = (rate == 0 ? block.timestamp : from) + secs and renew() passes from = d.leaseUntil, so a rate-0 (self-hosted) renew restarts from its own block and gives up the lead it landed with; only a paid renew extends from leaseUntil. The reserve sponsors a renew only when block.timestamp + renewWindow >= leaseUntil, so a sponsored rate-0 renew cycles at >= leaseSec - renewWindow (1500 s, 57.6/day at window 300); the old model under-budgeted rate-0 apps by ~17%.

model.renewalCadence({ leaseSec, rate6, renewW: NEW export. rate6 0 -> model 'rate-0', cycle = leaseSec - lead; rate6 > 0 -> 'paid', cycle = extensionSec (default leaseSec); rate6 null/undefined -> 'rate-unknown', the more frequent of both. Lead = explicit renewLeadSec (must be <= renewWindow when both given) else renewWindow (the earliest a sponsored renew may land = conservative); neither -> OwnerRefusal (no silent default). lead >= leaseSec -> OwnerRefusal{unbounded:true}. extension 1..leaseSec; explicit extension < minExtension refused; leaseSec < minExtension -> refused='ExtensionTooShort ...'.
model.renewalsFor(seconds, opts): paid n = ceil(T/ext) - 1 (unchanged formula); rate-0 n = ceil((T - leaseSec)/(leaseSec - lead)) for T > leaseSec; unknown = max. opts = renewalCadence inputs or its result. BREAKING-LOUDLY: the old shape renewalsFor(T, { leaseSec }) now throws OwnerRefusal (no rate-0 lead) instead of returning the 48/day count; a paid count renewalsFor(T, { leaseSec, rate6: >0 }) needs no lead.
model.renewsPerDay(opts): 86400 / cadence.cycleSec. BREAKING-LOUDLY: the old renewsPerDay(leaseSec) number argument throws OwnerRefusal ('different rates'). In-repo callers: costModel only.
model.knownRate6(st): NEW export: st.ledger.rate6 when the lease is live AND held by a runner (renewals use the claimed rate), else null (the next claim snapshots a new rate).
model.costModel(...): new optional inputs rate6 (default null = unknown, conservative), renewLeadSec, extensionSec; window from policy.renewWindow (< 30 = unconfigured reserve -> POLICY_DEFAULTS 300 and the basis says so); minExtension from policy. Output keeps every prior key (renewsPerDay, renewPerDayWei, renewalModel now = the cadence basis text) and adds `renewal` (the cadence). Window >= leaseSec: renewal.model 'unbounded', renewsPerDay/renewPerDayWei null (not a crash); an explicit invalid lead still throws.
model.advise(...): adds warns for cost.renewal.refused (ExtensionTooShort) and cost.renewal.unbounded; the runway warning now uses the corrected per-day wei.
model.budgetAmount(...): --days uses renewalsFor(N days, cost.renewal); refuses a cost without `renewal` (old shape), an unbounded cadence, or an ExtensionTooShort policy. Result adds `renewal` (model); basis text: 'one claim + N renewals (D days, leaseSec L; <cadence basis>) + one release at P wei/gas ...'.

Paid model assumes a compute balance that funds full quanta. Drip top-ups buy shorter extensions (bounded via extensionSec >= minExtension). The CLI does not expose extensionSec.
'Known' rate means the current live lease's. A re-claim by a different host can change the rate, so a paid budget does not cover a later switch to rate 0. An unknown rate is counted as rate 0.

The conservative rate-0 lead is the reserve window (300). The measured landing lead was <= 280 s, so the model over-counts by ~2.5% vs the median measured cycle. Hosts landing earlier than the window are impossible on the sponsored path but not on an operator-paid path, which this reserve never pays.
renewalsFor counts renewals needed to COVER the period from the claim. A continuously running host may send one more renew inside the last cycle; that is less than one renewal per budget.
